From tender to chewy
Nov 2019
I grew up in the States and had BBQ meat every weekend. I was in heaven when I found Quan Ut Ut serving smoky, slow-cooked rib that fall off the bone and melt in your mouth. But since earlier this year, the meat still fall off the bone but it's tough and chewy. 

I have been back several times hoping that this was just a fluke or mistake, but each time I ended up leaving most of the rib on the table and left with a tired jaw. 

Then this last time the manager finally told me that they have been getting their pork from Poland and many customers have complained the same as me.

Can we bring that juicy, tender, smoky, melt in your mouth rib back?

Perfect Ribs and Great Service
Aug 2019 • Couples
Quan Ut Ut serves great ribs, sausage, pulled meats, and other standard BBQ-style comfort foods in a comfortable, wide open venue. They do a nice job merging Vietnamese and Korean BBQ styles in a couple of their rib dishes. We, for example, had the Oh Heo Yeah ribs that are made with Vietnamese fish sauce. They were perfect - great flavor and fall-off-the-bone meat. Quan Ut Ut also serves local beers on tap from Biacraft, and their service is excellent. If you need a break from noodles and you like BBQ, head to Quan Ut Ut.

Reasonable Meal at Quan Ut UT
Mar 2019 • Friends
I must admit that for me this restaurant would lie between a Good and Very Good but as the rating doesn't allow for this then I would lean towards the Very Good. The staff are super friendly and attentive which makes for a very pleasant experience and willingly supply fans pointed at the table if the customers request them. Other wise some days this open air restaurant could be quite unbearable. My husband enjoyed the ribs, as did a couple of friends but he said he would order dryer ribs next time with out all the sauce which he felt detracted somewhat from the tasty meat. The french fries were thin shoestring style but thank fully were nice and hot, not warm as is usual with thin french fries. The burger was a delightful surprise, the best I have found in Ho Chi Minh so far - tasty and cooked exactly as asked for. The coleslaw wasn't particularly tasty which was rather disappointing but the potato salad was good and the dressing on the side of salad. The buttered sweet corn was very good indeed. I have eaten many times in the D1 branch and had some excellent meals so maybe I had unrealistic hope for this newer branch. However I would definitely go there again and try some different combinations.

Delicious BBQ in district 2
Dec 2018 • Friends
A local friend brought me here on my first night back in HCMc. It is large bbq restaurant with huge outdoor dining & cooking area as well as an indoor area. The outdoor area easily converts to indoor by the use of a automatic roof which is handy for the Saigon weather. The menu is incredibly broad and mouth watering: everything from fresh oysters from Nha Trang to a variety of hamburgers to spicy Italian sausages and shoulders of lamb and more! This is seriously a meat eaters heaven. Along with this are a nice selection of boutique and craft beers.

The two of us ate and drank till we were totally full and it came to approx just under a 1million. Vnd which is easily half of what it would have cost to eat the same meal back home in Sydney. Well worth a visit for tourists wanting meat dishes with a western slant.

So we order 3 courses for dinner and they were really bad. The pork BBQ was bad, too much juicy.

The Australian steak was disaster, we ordered medium rare but then came out half meidum on the left and half rare on the right (they cut the steak for us already). Excuses me. I want medium rare, not medium|rare, and they gave us a big part of the tendon and was too hard either too rare (picture). 

The waiter explained me because I ordered medium rare so this is it. Forgot to mentioned he said there would be pickle or some kind of vegetables went along with the steak but actually it didn't. 

If you looking for a palce to chit chat with friend and have some beer and don't mind about the quality of foods. It just may be the place. But we will never return.
